newsitem.title: FRANCE: Guillen, Bernard named to Bank of France council.
newsitem.headline: Guillen, Bernard named to Bank of France council.

text.p: The French government announced on Friday that Pierre Guillen and Jean-Rene Bernard would be named members of the Bank of France's monetary policy council, in a move which could tip the balance of power at the central bank.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said that Guillen and Bernard would replace ex-journalist Jean Boissonnat and ex-banker Bruno de Maulde, whose mandates expire next week, on the nine-member council.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe said the appointments did not imply any change in policy direction.

Economists had said, however, the appointements of the two men, flagged by press reports earlier, could possibly eventually shift the bias in the council towards cutting interest rates faster to boost growth and reduce high unemployment.

The move would give President Jacques Chirac, who sources say personally supported Guillen and Bernard, considerable leverage over the Bank of France's council, until now dominated by its governor Jean-Claude Trichet, economists have said.

Both Boissonnat and de Maulde were believed to be part of a six-to-three majority in favour of the existing policy of maintaining a premium of French rates over German rates to defend the stability of the franc-mark exchange rate.
Guillen, 69, is a former head of the CNPF employers' assocation, while Bernard, 64, has worked in both the state administration and in state-sector companies.
